claims.text: The rider's claim is proven on the platform's own trace: the GPS polyline between the recorded pickup and dropoff events measures 30.94 km against a booked optimal of 23.8 km, an excess of 7.14 km. That excess is 30.0% of the optimal distance, which clears the 20% establishment test, and 7.14 km is far above the 0.8 km absolute test, so both limbs of POL-RD-01 pass and the deviation is ESTABLISHED. The trace figure governs over the rounded trip_record copy of 30.9 km, exactly as POL-RD-01 requires.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-02834 and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-18T10:10:16+08:00 matches the trip_record's started_at, so the artifacts describe the same trip; and the excess of 7.14 km / 30.0% meets the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from a trace that is unimpaired (100.0% coverage, 243 fixes at a 10 s interval, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0). The burden therefore shifts to the driver.

The driver's only answer is 'Followed navigation.' That is a general assertion of good driving, not a specific artifact-and-clause invocation. POL-RD-08 requires the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12; an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. No exculpatory clause is available on this record.

The driver cannot fall back on an external traffic cause. The bundle holds no traffic advisory covering this trip window: EV-ADVIS-02834-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and its issue detail records that no advisory covers the Northpoint City corridor in this window. Under POL-RD-13 the traffic assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else, that comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight. The deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any of the excess. The chat log for this trip is empty - 0 messages, first_message_at and last_message_at both null - so there is no rider instruction recorded, no waypoint_hint to test, and POL-RD-04(a) to (c) cannot be satisfied. The driver's 'followed navigation' statement is not a rider instruction and does not engage the clause.

No relocation of the pickup or dropoff point rescues the driver either. The trip_record shows original_pickup and original_dropoff both null, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null. POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-quote against, so the booked optimal of 23.8 km stands as the baseline.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. The fare model is METERED and the surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown is 1.0. Recomputed fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 23.8 + 0.28 x 32.1) x 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 31.4380. Refund = charged_total 39.06 - 31.4380 = 7.6220, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 7.65. That is 19.5% of the charged total, well below the 90% full-refund share, and above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 7.65.

The rider should not be left paying for gantries he never crossed, but on this record there is nothing to correct: the fare_breakdown carries zero ERP lines, erp_gantries is empty, and the off-optimal-route and on-optimal-route ERP totals are both 0.00. No standalone pass-through correction under POL-RD-09 arises, and the POL-RD-02 figure above already comprehends all distance and time charges.

The driver's profile does not aggravate this case, and I do not overstate it. The deviation is MATERIAL (30.0% exceeds the 50% materiality test? No - it does not: 30.0% is below 50% and 7.14 km is below 8.0 km, so the deviation is established but NOT material). POL-RD-06 is therefore not triggered, and the driver's deviation_flags_90d of 0 would in any event fail the pattern test. The rider's own profile is likewise clean: deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift for a serial claimant does not apply.

The trace is clean for policy purposes and no escalation trigger fires. Coverage is 100.0%, there are 243 fixes at a 10 s sample interval against an expected 10 s, gaps is empty and max_gap_sec is 0.0, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the timestamps do not run backwards, and the refund of 7.65 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total. The case is decidable on the record and should be ruled, not escalated.

The rider's excess is therefore measured from the trace itself.

No rider-requested detour can be read into this record. The chat log for this trip carries zero messages, so there is no rider instruction, no waypoint_hint and no named road; POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable. The excess is not excluded on that ground.

No relocation of the pickup or dropoff point rescues the driver either. The trip_record shows original_pickup and original_dropoff both null, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share.

No ERP or surcharge correction is due on top of that figure. The fare_breakdown carries zero ERP lines with an off-optimal-route total of 0.00 and an on-optimal-route total of 0.00, no airport surcharge, and no tolls, so there is no pass-through line to refund separately under POL-RD-09 and nothing to add to the POL-RD-02 amount.

The driver's profile does not establish a repeat deviation pattern, and I do not claim one. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 326, so neither the count of 3 or more nor the 0.05 ratio test in POL-RD-06 is met. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 asks for. The remedy is therefore the POL-RD-02 partial refund, not the POL-RD-06(b) uplift.

The rider's profile likewise neither helps nor hurts the claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration trigger for a claim below 30% excess does not fire, and no other field on that profile may ground a finding under POL-GEN-01.

The rider's own claim text overstates the distance at 30.94 km for 23.8 km and the fare at $39.06, but the excess it describes is real and the arithmetic refund is 7.65, not the full 6.00 the rider contested. I do not stretch the record to the rider's figure: the refund is the POL-RD-02 computation on the trace as measured.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your claim is upheld in part, and SGD 7.65 of the SGD 39.06 you were charged is returned to you. To the driver: the charge stands for the distance actually and lawfully driven, but not for the excess. This ruling was made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days (POL-GEN-04).

THE DEVIATION IS ESTABLISHED. POL-RD-01 requires the threshold test to be run on the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy: EV-GPS-02834 measures 30.94 km of polyline between the recorded pickup and dropoff events, and the booked optimal on EV-TRIP-02834 is 23.8 km, so the excess is 7.14 km. That is 30.0% of optimal, clearing the 20% limb, and it clears the 0.8 km absolute limb, so both establishment tests pass and a route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence. It is NOT a material deviation: 7.14 km is below the 8.0 km mark and 30.0% is below the 50% mark, so POL-RD-06 is never engaged, no repeat-pattern finding is made, and no driver-conduct referral arises. The trace is clean for policy purposes as well as for the pre-pass — 243 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s — so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) do not fire and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

BURDEN. The rider discharged the POL-RD-08 initial burden: EV-TRIP-02834, EV-GPS-02834 and EV-FARE-02834 all carry trip TRP-02834, the trace's first fix at 10:10:16 matches the recorded start, and the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The driver's only answer, 'Followed navigation', cites no artifact and no clause and does not discharge the shifted burden. There is also no traffic advisory to run: EV-ADVIS-02834-01 is MISSING at weight_multiplier 0.0 (its issue is MISSING_ARTIFACT — no advisory covers the Northpoint City corridor in this window), so POL-RD-03 has nothing behind it and the driver's general assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. This is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation: no exculpatory clause was invoked against a cited artifact by the party relying on it, and the absence of an advisory nobody relied on is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it — precisely the situation POL-RD-13 addresses.

NO EXONERATION. The chat log EV-CHAT-02834 carries 0 messages, so no rider instruction under POL-RD-04 exists and no waypoint_hint is available to corroborate one. EV-TRIP-02834 shows original_pickup and original_dropoff null, both amendment timestamps null and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-05 has no re-quote to run and the booked optimal of 23.8 km stands.

THE REFUND IS ARITHMETIC. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs. The surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-02834 and is 1.0. Recomputed fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 23.8 km = 17.85 + 0.28 x 32.1 min = 8.988) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP/tolls + 0.00 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 31.4380. Charged total = 39.06. Refund = 39.06 - 31.4380 = 7.6220, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 7.65. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and 19.5% of the charged total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. POL-RD-09 adds nothing: EV-FARE-02834 carries zero ERP lines (off-route total 0.00, on-route total 0.00) and no airport surcharge, so there is no pass-through correction and no billing-integrity referral. The driver is owed no compensation either: the rider was billed 30.9 km against a trace of 30.94 km, a shortfall of 0.04 km, far below the 1.0 km that POL-RD-04's compensation limb requires.

The rider's claim text ('30.94 km for 23.8 km, $39.06') describes the excess correctly, but the amount returned is the arithmetic figure of 7.65, not a round estimate, and it is taken from the fare breakdown's refund computation. The driver's advocate is right that the excess is real and the refund is the POL-RD-02 figure, and that concession is accepted.

DISCARDED EVIDENCE. Two claims about the missing advisory were discarded at the mechanical citation check because each cited EV-ADVIS-02834-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) without disclosing the impairment as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. Nothing in this ruling rests on that artifact.
